title: Real-time EEG feedback on alpha power lateralization leads to behavioral improvements in a covert attention task
description: EEG recordings from fourteen healthy participants performing a covert spatial attention task across three sessions. The study tested real-time feedback of alpha power lateralization (α-LI) versus sham feedback in a single-blinded crossover design. It examined whether such neurofeedback leads to behavioral improvements in attention.
methods_description: 64-channel active g.tec HIamp EEG recorded at 512 Hz, referenced to linked ears, with electrodes placed per the 10-10 system and ground at FCz. Three sessions on separate days: day one had practice and four offline calibration runs; days two and three had offline runs plus real-time or sham α-LI feedback runs in a crossover design. Participants responded to target-offset events with a right index finger button press.
